title: Dx.Cli
proposition: Apply deterministic workspace changes without accepting partial state.
story: Dx.Cli is a .NET command-line tool that applies deterministic workspace-change packages transactionally while preserving inspectable state. Its installed dxs command initializes workspaces, applies validated changes and manages snapshots, diffs, checkout, logs, sessions, packing and diagnostics.
contribution: I designed the command workflow, separated the Spectre.Console interface from core execution authority, and implemented locking, atomic commits, rollback, interrupted-transaction recovery, SQLite metadata and content-addressed storage.

reflection.summary: Developer tooling becomes more trustworthy when parsing, validation, planning, execution and recovery share one explicit authority rather than several convenient mutation paths.

limitations: The run, eval, configuration, and session creation and closure commands are prototype-gated and unavailable.
Successful publication through NuGet, GitHub Releases, WinGet or Homebrew is not established.
Production readiness, external adoption and distributed transaction guarantees are not established.

provenance.description: Mechanically derived from the controlling public projection.
